points: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah. His mother was a harlot, but he himself was a mighty man of valour.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Gilead's wife's sons grew up and thrust out Jephthah: thou shalt not inherit in our father's house, for thou art the son of a strange woman. Strange woman here does not mean his mother was of another nation; the scripture says only that she was a harlot. His brothers cast him out of his father's house over his mother, though he had as much right to that house as they did.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah fled from his brethren and dwelt in the land of Tob, and there were gathered vain men to Jephthah, and went out with him. Watch what that shows: when we do our brothers and sisters wrong, when the ones trying to do right do not get the love and support they need from their own family, they go looking for love in the wrong places, and you see the kind of men they gravitate to.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: In process of time the children of Ammon made war against Israel, and the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob: come and be our captain, that we may fight with the children of Ammon. Now they wanted the man of valour they had cast out.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah answered, Did not ye hate me, and expel me out of my father's house? and why are ye come unto me now when ye are in distress? You hated me, you put me out, and now that trouble has come, you need me.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and captain over them: and Jephthah uttered all his words before the LORD in Mizpeh.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah sent messengers unto the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come against me to fight in my land? He wanted to know what Ammon had against Israel.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: The king of Ammon answered, Because Israel took away my land, when they came up out of Egypt, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and unto Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably. That claim was a lie, and Jephthah knew it.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah sent messengers again and broke down the whole history: Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon. He knew the record, so nobody could talk him out of it.

This is why we must know our history. The king of Ammon could have pulled that on somebody ignorant and been given the land; Jephthah said no, that is not what happened, the book of Numbers does not say that. People try to confuse us about the Bible in the street the same way, so prepare yourself to the search of the fathers.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Howbeit the king of the children of Ammon hearkened not unto the words of Jephthah: the Lord had hardened their hearts not to listen, the same as he did with Sihon.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over unto the children of Ammon.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah came to Mizpeh unto his house, and behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances; and she was his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: And it was a custom in Israel, that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: The men of Ephraim gathered themselves together and went northward and said unto Jephthah, Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didst not call us to go with thee? we will burn thine house upon thee with fire. They came at their own deliverer with a threat.
Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead and fought with Ephraim, and the men of Gilead smote Ephraim and took the passages of Jordan before the Ephraimites.
Jephthah judged Israel six years; then died Jephthah the Gileadite, and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.

So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord
